MetaPrediction
An Earth System Hypothesis Discovery Engine

Earth observation missions generate enormous amounts of data, yet connecting diverse datasets and transforming complex patterns into testable scientific hypotheses remains challenging.

To address this, Team Hypatia developed Meta Prediction, an Earth System Hypothesis Discovery Engine that moves beyond forecasting toward scientific discovery. It integrates Earth observation data, investigates relationships across space and time, identifies changing patterns, and produces candidate hypotheses and interpretable mathematical models for evaluation.

We demonstrated the engine by investigating relationships between El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) variability and rainfall across three Indonesian regions, using NASA GPM IMERG precipitation data and NOAA's RONI index. Our analysis identified seasonal and regional patterns, generated a candidate hypothesis, and evaluated a mathematical model against observed rainfall.

Meta Prediction aims to help researchers, scientists, and educators explore complex datasets, identify meaningful relationships, formulate testable research questions, and unlock greater scientific value from NASA's Earth observation data.
details:
Project Details

Meta Prediction

Meta Prediction is an Earth System Hypothesis Discovery Engine developed by Team Hypatia to help transform complex Earth observation data into meaningful scientific insights, interpretable mathematical relationships, and testable hypotheses.

How It Works

The engine integrates and processes Earth observation datasets, aligns observations across time and geographical regions, and investigates statistical relationships, seasonal variations, time lags, and recurring or changing patterns.

It then supports the formulation of candidate scientific hypotheses, develops interpretable mathematical models, and evaluates their performance against observed data. Through interactive visualizations and dynamic networks, users can explore the relationships identified by the analysis.

Scientific Demonstration

Our demonstration investigates the relationship between El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) variability in the tropical Pacific and rainfall across three regions of Indonesia.

We use NASA GPM IMERG precipitation data and NOAA's Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI).

The analysis identifies seasonal and regional relationships, produces a candidate scientific hypothesis, and evaluates a mathematical model against observed rainfall. Importantly, the system distinguishes statistically supported findings from results that remain uncertain or require further validation.

Tools and Technologies

The prototype was developed using Python for scientific data processing, statistical analysis, and mathematical modeling. Streamlit provides the interactive web interface, while GitHub supports source-code management and collaboration.

The project uses publicly available NASA and NOAA scientific datasets. Development and testing were conducted in a software-based environment using standard computing hardware, without requiring specialized physical equipment.

Innovation and Creativity

Unlike conventional forecasting applications, Meta Prediction focuses on scientific exploration and hypothesis generation.

Its proposed G-NETS (Global Non-linear Earth Topology Systems) framework introduces a network-based approach for examining how relationships between Earth-system variables may change across regions, seasons, and time periods.

The project combines data analysis, mathematical modeling, scientific reasoning, and interactive visualization within a single research-oriented workflow.

Benefits and Expected Impact

Meta Prediction aims to help researchers, scientists, and educators investigate complex Earth datasets more efficiently, discover relationships worth further study, and formulate scientifically testable research questions.

Its long-term potential includes supporting scientific exploration across different Earth-system domains and enhancing the research value of NASA's Earth observation data.

Scientific Considerations

Our team prioritized data provenance, interpretability, statistical reliability, uncertainty, and scientific transparency.

We recognize that statistical association does not establish causation, candidate hypotheses require rigorous testing, and mathematical models must be evaluated against appropriate baselines.

Rather than presenting every detected pattern as a discovery, Meta Prediction is designed to support evidence-based scientific investigation and clearly communicate the limitations of its findings.
